23 Which statement about waves is correct?
A
Both longitudinal and transverse waves can travel through a vacuum.
B
Both longitudinal and transverse waves transfer matter.
C
Longitudinal progressive waves consist of alternate nodes and antinodes.
D
The particles of a transverse wave vibrate perpendicular to the direction of energy
propagation.

hints: Look at the words vacuum in A and matter in B. Ask yourself which waves need a material medium and what a wave actually carries from place to place.
Recall the defining test for longitudinal versus transverse: compare the direction of particle vibration with the direction of energy propagation.
Recall the difference between progressive and stationary waves. Ask where fixed nodes and antinodes are found.
walkthrough: List what each statement claims: A is about travel through a vacuum, B is about transfer of matter, C links progressive waves to nodes and antinodes, D links transverse vibration direction to energy direction.

State the governing rules: mechanical waves need a medium, so longitudinal sound cannot cross a vacuum while transverse electromagnetic waves can; all waves transfer energy not matter; nodes and antinodes occur only in stationary waves.
Check A and B against those rules. A is false because longitudinal waves cannot travel through a vacuum, and B is false because particles oscillate about equilibrium with no net motion of matter.
Check C. A longitudinal progressive wave consists of travelling compressions and rarefactions, not fixed nodes where amplitude is always zero and antinodes where it is maximum.

Check D. By definition, in a transverse wave the oscillations are perpendicular to energy transfer, while in a longitudinal wave they are parallel. This matches the statement exactly. This is option D.

A.explanation: Only transverse electromagnetic waves can travel through a vacuum. Longitudinal waves such as sound need particles of a medium to compress and rarefy.

B.explanation: All progressive waves transfer energy without net transfer of matter. The particles oscillate about fixed mean positions.

C.explanation: Alternate nodes and antinodes are a property of stationary waves, not progressive waves which show moving compressions or crests.

D.explanation: This is the definition of a transverse wave. Particle vibration is at $90^{\circ}$ to the direction in which energy is transferred.
